roe.equation: core PAT / average equity (share capital + reserves)

band.rationale: ROE below the cost of equity destroys value; 5pp above it is clear value creation. Ke = rf + beta x ERP (config/market.yaml).

roce.name: Return on capital employed
roce.equation: EBIT / average (equity + borrowings), EBIT = core PBT + interest
roce.meaning: Pre-tax operating return on all funding (Screener's definition).

band.rationale: ROCE is pre-tax, so the hurdle is the pre-tax WACC.

roic.name: Return on invested capital
roic.equation: NOPAT / average IC; NOPAT = (EBITDA - Dep) x (1 - ETR), ETR = core tax / core PBT clipped 0-40% (statutory if PBT <= 0); IC = equity + borrowings - cash - investments (+ manual minority interest); n/m if IC <= 0
roic.meaning: After-tax operating return on the capital actually tied up in operations (excludes cash, investments and the income they earn).

band.rationale: ROIC below WACC destroys value; 5pp above it is clear value creation.

attributable_factor.name: Attributable-profit factor
attributable_factor.meaning: Owners' share of after-tax profit: below 1 = minorities take a slice; above 1 = associate/JV income adds to it.

tax_burden.name: Tax burden
tax_burden.meaning: Share of pre-tax profit kept after tax (1 - effective tax rate).

interest_burden.name: Interest burden
interest_burden.meaning: Share of EBIT left after interest.

equity_multiplier.name: Equity multiplier
equity_multiplier.meaning: Assets per rupee of equity: the leverage term in DuPont.

debt_to_equity_avg.name: Borrowings / equity (average)
debt_to_equity_avg.meaning: Debt part of the equity multiplier.

other_liab_to_equity_avg.name: Other liabilities / equity (average)
other_liab_to_equity_avg.meaning: Non-debt liabilities part of the equity multiplier.

nopat_margin.name: NOPAT margin
nopat_margin.meaning: After-tax operating profit per rupee of revenue (the margin half of ROIC).

reinvestment_rate.name: Reinvestment rate
reinvestment_rate.equation: (Capex proxy - Depreciation + change in NWC) / NOPAT (NOPAT > 0); NWC = other assets - cash - other liabilities
reinvestment_rate.meaning: Share of after-tax operating profit ploughed back into fixed assets and working capital. Good only if incremental ROIC exceeds WACC.

payout_ratio.name: Dividend payout
payout_ratio.meaning: Share of core profit paid as dividends (Screener 'Dividend Amount', declared for the year).

share_count_change.name: Share count change
share_count_change.meaning: Net issuance (dilution, +) or buyback (-) of shares, adjusted for splits and bonuses.

band.rationale: Net issuance above 3% a year is material dilution; flat or falling share count = no dilution/buybacks.

share_count_change.text: Share count change: 0.0% AMBER (level green vs indicative band (green <= 0.0%, red >= 3.0%); trend stable +0.0pp/yr; volatile (CV 0.57))

buyback_estimate.name: Buyback (estimate)
buyback_estimate.equation: max(0, -(Adj shares_t - Adj shares_t-1)) x (Price_t + Price_t-1)/2
buyback_estimate.meaning: Estimated rupees spent on buybacks: shares retired x average of the two year-end prices.

shareholder_yield.name: Shareholder yield
shareholder_yield.meaning: Cash returned to shareholders (dividends + estimated buybacks) as a share of year-end market value.

dividend_to_fcf.name: Dividends / FCF
dividend_to_fcf.equation: Dividend / (CFO - capex proxy); 99 if FCF <= 0 and dividend > 0; 0 if no dividend
dividend_to_fcf.meaning: Dividends relative to free cash flow: above 1 = payouts funded from the balance sheet (99 = dividend paid with FCF <= 0).

band.rationale: Paying out more than 120% of FCF must be funded by cash reserves or debt; under 70% leaves room to reinvest.

net_debt_to_ebitda.meaning: Years of operating profit needed to repay net debt (negative = net cash). Borrowings include lease liabilities.

band.rationale: S&P Corporate Methodology financial-risk benchmarks (standard volatility): debt/EBITDA < 1.5x minimal, 1.5-2x modest, 2-3x intermediate, 3-4x significant, 4-5x aggressive, > 5x highly leveraged (summary: https://ibinterviewquestions.com/guides/debt-capital-markets/rating-methodology-how-agencies-score-credit). Engine uses net debt, so the band is slightly lenient.

interest_cover.name: Interest cover
interest_cover.equation: EBIT / Interest, EBIT = core PBT + interest; = 99 if interest ~ 0; clipped to [-99, 99]
interest_cover.meaning: How many times EBIT covers interest (capped at 99x when interest is negligible).

band.rationale: Damodaran synthetic rating (large non-financial firms, Jan 2026): coverage < 2.5x maps below BBB (sub-investment grade); >= 4.25x maps to A or better.

interest_cover.text: Interest cover: 34.99x GREEN (level green vs band (red <= 2.50x, green >= 4.25x); trend deteriorating -18.82x/yr; moderate (CV 0.36))

current_ratio_proxy.name: Current ratio (Screener proxy)
current_ratio_proxy.meaning: Short-term liquidity proxy: the export has no current/non-current split, so (other assets + investments) / other liabilities is used. Investments are included because Indian companies hold treasury mainly in liquid funds and bonds, which Screener reports under Investments, not Cash. Excludes short-term debt (inside Borrowings).

band.rationale: Textbook liquidity norm: below 1.0x short-term obligations exceed short-term assets; 1.5x+ is comfortable. Proxy excludes short-term debt.

cash_to_st_borrowings.name: Cash and investments / short-term borrowings
cash_to_st_borrowings.equation: (Cash & bank + Investments) / short-term borrowings (manual) or / Borrowings; = 99 when there is no debt
cash_to_st_borrowings.meaning: Liquid cover for debt falling due soon: cash plus investments (treasury is mostly held in liquid funds and bonds, reported under Investments). Uses manual short_term_borrowings when supplied, otherwise total borrowings (conservative: treats all debt as short-term).

band.rationale: Cash covering all short-term debt (1.0x) removes refinancing risk; under 0.2x depends on rollovers.

debt_vs_ebitda_growth.name: Debt growth - EBITDA growth
debt_vs_ebitda_growth.equation: (Borrowings_t/Borrowings_t-1 - 1) - (EBITDA_t/EBITDA_t-1 - 1); n/m if prior debt < 1% of assets or prior EBITDA <= 0
debt_vs_ebitda_growth.meaning: Debt growing faster than the profit that services it (n/m when debt was negligible).

band.rationale: Debt growing 10pp a year faster than EBITDA erodes coverage quickly.

altman_x4.name: Altman Z'' X4

band.rationale: Altman (2005), Emerging Markets Review 6(4): EM score = Z'' + 3.25; Z'' zones safe > 2.6, distress < 1.1 => EM score safe > 5.85, distress < 4.35. Engine uses Screener proxies (see docs/methodology.md).

cfo_to_ebitda.name: CFO / EBITDA
cfo_to_ebitda.meaning: How much of operating profit arrives as operating cash (after working capital and tax).

band.rationale: After tax (~25%) and normal working-capital needs, 80%+ of EBITDA should arrive as CFO; below 50% means profit is being absorbed by working capital.

cfo_to_ebitda.text: CFO / EBITDA: 0.73 GREEN (level amber vs indicative band (red <= 0.50, green >= 0.80); trend stable 0.02/yr; stable (CV 0.14))

fcf_to_pat.name: FCF / PAT
fcf_to_pat.meaning: Free cash flow per rupee of core profit in the year.

band.rationale: Single-year FCF is lumpy (capex cycles), hence the wide amber zone; use the 5-year version for judgement.

fcf_to_pat.text: FCF / PAT: 0.57 RED (level amber vs indicative band (red <= 0.20, green >= 0.80); trend deteriorating -0.04/yr; volatile (CV 7.30))

fcf_to_pat_5y.name: FCF / PAT (5y cumulative)
fcf_to_pat_5y.meaning: Free cash flow conversion over a full cycle (5 years), smoothing lumpy capex.

band.rationale: Over a cycle, a mature business should convert 70%+ of profit into free cash; below 30% profit is being reinvested or is not real.

fcf_to_pat_5y.text: FCF / PAT (5y cumulative): 0.87 GREEN (level green vs indicative band (red <= 0.30, green >= 0.70); trend improving 0.29/yr; volatile (CV 2.55))

cfo_to_pat_5y.name: CFO / PAT (5y cumulative)
cfo_to_pat_5y.meaning: Operating cash flow conversion of profits over 5 years: below 60% means profits are not turning into cash.

band.rationale: Cumulative CFO below 60% of cumulative PAT over 5 years is the red-flag threshold in the brief; 90%+ = profits are cash-backed.

cfo_to_pat_5y.text: CFO / PAT (5y cumulative): 1.11 GREEN (level green vs indicative band (red <= 0.60, green >= 0.90); trend stable 0.02/yr; stable (CV 0.04))

accruals_ratio.name: Accruals ratio
accruals_ratio.meaning: Profit not backed by operating cash, scaled by assets (Sloan-style total accruals): high = lower-quality earnings.

band.rationale: Sloan (1996), The Accounting Review 71(3): firms in the extreme accrual decile (accruals around 10%+ of assets) have lower subsequent earnings persistence and returns. Negative accruals (cash > profit) = green.

accruals_ratio.text: Accruals ratio: 5.1% RED (level amber vs band (green <= 0.0%, red >= 10.0%); trend deteriorating +0.9pp/yr; volatile (CV 0.73))

receivables_vs_revenue_growth.name: Receivables growth - revenue growth
receivables_vs_revenue_growth.equation: (Rec_t / Rec_t-1 - 1) - (Rev_t / Rev_t-1 - 1); n/m if prior receivables < 0.5% of revenue
receivables_vs_revenue_growth.meaning: Receivables growing faster than sales can signal channel stuffing, looser credit or collection problems.

band.rationale: Receivables outgrowing revenue by 10pp+ in a year is a classic quality warning (Beneish DSRI logic).

receivables_vs_revenue_growth.text: Receivables growth - revenue growth: -16.6pp GREEN (level green vs indicative band (green <= +0.0pp, red >= +10.0pp); trend improving -5.8pp/yr; volatile (CV 2.62))

exceptional_frequency_5y.name: Exceptional items frequency (5y)
exceptional_frequency_5y.equation: count over last 5 years of [|estimated exceptional| > 5% x |PBT|]
exceptional_frequency_5y.meaning: In how many of the last 5 years profit contained a material exceptional item (|item| > 5% of PBT).

band.rationale: One exceptional year in five is normal; three or more means 'exceptional' items are recurring.

exceptional_frequency_5y.text: Exceptional items frequency (5y): 1 AMBER (level green vs indicative band (green <= 1, red >= 3); trend deteriorating 0/yr)

exceptional_size_5y.name: Exceptional items size (5y)
exceptional_size_5y.meaning: How big exceptional items were relative to profit over 5 years.

beneish_dsri.name: Beneish DSRI
beneish_dsri.meaning: Days-sales-in-receivables index: receivables/sales this year vs last.

beneish_gmi.name: Beneish GMI
beneish_gmi.meaning: Gross-margin index: last year's gross margin / this year's (>1 = deteriorating margins).

beneish_aqi.name: Beneish AQI
beneish_aqi.equation: [1 - (CA_t + NB_t)/TA_t] / [1 - (CA_t-1 + NB_t-1)/TA_t-1], CA proxy = receivables + inventory + cash
beneish_aqi.meaning: Asset-quality index: share of 'soft' assets (not current assets or net block) this year vs last.

beneish_depi.name: Beneish DEPI
beneish_depi.equation: DepRate_t-1 / DepRate_t, DepRate = Dep / (Dep + Net block)
beneish_depi.meaning: Depreciation index: last year's depreciation rate / this year's (>1 = slower depreciation).

beneish_sgai.name: Beneish SGAI
beneish_sgai.equation: (SGA_t/Sales_t) / (SGA_t-1/Sales_t-1), SGA proxy = selling & admin + other expenses (other opex if that is <= 0)
beneish_sgai.meaning: SG&A index: SG&A/sales this year vs last.

beneish_lvgi.name: Beneish LVGI
beneish_lvgi.meaning: Leverage index: (debt + other liabilities)/assets this year vs last.

beneish_m_score.name: Beneish M-score (Screener proxies)
beneish_m_score.meaning: Probability-style earnings-manipulation screen (Beneish 1999, 8 variables) built from Screener line items. Above -1.78 = profile resembles known manipulators; a screen, not proof.

band.rationale: Beneish (1999), Financial Analysts Journal 55(5): 8-variable M-score; above -1.78 classifies as a likely manipulator. -2.22 is the stricter cut-off used in later work (Beneish, Lee & Nichols 2013, FAJ 69(2), https://doi.org/10.2469/faj.v69.n2.1).

sector.how_to_read:
FMCG value comes from volume growth at stable gross margins, funded by suppliers and distributors (negative working capital).
Split revenue growth into volume and price/mix: price-led growth without volume is borrowed from the future.
Gross margin should hold through commodity swings (pass-through); A&P spend is the reinvestment in the brand, so a margin
gain made by cutting A&P is low quality. Returns are very high because capital needs are tiny: watch for acquisitions diluting ROIC.

Screener puts exceptional items inside Other Income (PBT = Sales - Expenses + Other income - Dep - Interest holds exactly). Other income is split into core and estimated exceptional (see 'exceptional').

Capex is not in the export. Proxy = change in net block + change in CWIP + depreciation (includes acquired fixed assets and Ind AS 116 right-of-use additions; impairments and disposals understate it). FCF = CFO - capex proxy.
Current price and market cap are as of the export date, which the file does not record (latest quarter in file: 2026-09-30).

Balance-sheet step change: total assets +241% in one year (acquisition, consolidation change or large capital raise). Growth across FY20->FY21 may not be organic.
